admission.justification: Checked call records were chosen over disabling logging, moving it outside observation or excluding logs wholesale, because those alternatives would conceal required telemetry or unruled product writes in future read-only proofs.

alternatives.option: Preserve and validate the daily tool-log and completed-call river records while comparing all other product state.
alternatives.reason: A call remains observed and unrelated product writes remain detectable.

alternatives.option: Disable the log, move its transcript root outside coordination, skip tests or exclude the logs tree wholesale.
alternatives.reason: The packet and first ruling explicitly reject these ways of obtaining a green comparison because they remove observation and can hide mutations.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only if the owning requirement authority deliberately retires these call records or changes the required installation layout and observation contract.

alternatives.option: Admit the workspace event by name without checking it.
alternatives.reason: The river ruling requires byte-prefix, actual completed-call tool accounting and a rewritten-earlier-event negative case; mere exclusion does not prove a record of the call.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only if the owning authority changes the completed-call event contract and supplies an alternative proof that detects unexpected writes.

consequences: Registered read-only proofs distinguish product publication from required telemetry and validate admitted records instead of hiding them.
An unruled third product write remains a finding routed to its code/requirement owner, never permission to expand the allowlist.
context: A registered preview cannot be proved read-only by universal root equality after daily tool logging and completed-answer events became required call records. MIK-R131 rule8 and the river ruling preserve those producers while bounding the proof.
